sections.html:
Milwaukee County deeds and mortgages are filed with the Register of Deeds, Room 103 at 901 N. 9th Street, Milwaukee, WI 53233. You can drop papers off or mail them. The counter runs 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. on weekdays; call (414) 278-4021.

Deeds are one task among several. Staff also scan and index corporation papers and military discharges, log informal probate instruments, hold financing statements, collect the transfer fee and issue birth, death and marriage certificates.

Roughly 924,216 people lived here as of July 1, 2025, every one inside a city or village, because no unincorporated towns exist in this county. A single office serves all 19 municipalities, 10 cities and 9 villages.

Filing an ordinary document is $30 however many pages it runs. Plats, certified copies and the sale transfer fee are billed on top. The counter takes cash, checks and money orders payable to the Register of Deeds, and no credit or debit cards.

Document or serviceCost
Standard document (not a plat)$30
Certified copy bought at recording$2 first page, $1 each added page, $1 to certify
Subdivision plat$50
Condominium plat$100 review (separate check) plus $50 recording
Department of Transportation plat$25
Termination of decedent's interest$30

Anything else sent in with a plat is charged the standard $30 apiece. For a sale, the receipt for your transfer return shows the fee, which you settle at the counter together with recording.

sections.h2: How the transfer fee is figured
sections.html:
Here is the math. A non-exempt conveyance owes 30 cents on each $100 of value, with any leftover fraction treated as a whole $100. Put another way, $3 per $1,000. Wis. Stat. 77.22 assigns it to the seller (the grantor), and staff take payment at the moment the deed arrives.

Value is whatever was paid or will be paid, liens included. A gift, a token-price deed or a swap is measured instead by the likely open market price between a willing buyer and a willing seller (s. 77.21). The county retains 20 percent of its collections and forwards the balance to the state (s. 77.24).

Section 77.25 carves out exemptions. People selling or inheriting a house see these the most:

  • Property passing by will, descent or survivorship.
  • A lender or land contract vendor taking title through foreclosure or a deed in lieu.
  • Tax and assessment sale deeds.
  • Gifts within the family, like parent to child, stepparent to stepchild or grandparent to grandchild, given for little or nothing.
  • Property of $1,000 or less in value.
  • Paperwork whose only purpose is to secure or release a debt.

Staff won't rule on whether your exemption holds, so describe it correctly on the return. Local governments may not layer their own charge on a conveyance the state fee exempts (s. 77.256).

Pack three things: the signed original deed, the transfer return receipt and your payment. Section 77.22(2) requires the return with every conveyance, and without it the register refuses the deed. The Department of Revenue hosts the return in My Tax Account, and no username or password is needed to file.

  • The original deed, finished before it is handed in.
  • The return receipt, or the exemption reason printed on it.
  • Cash or a check to the Register of Deeds covering $30 and whatever transfer fee applies.
  • Your name and address as the return recipient, because the original is posted back to you.

Wis. Stat. 706.05 sets the content rules. The deed needs the signatures the law demands and enough description of land and parties for the office to index it. Papers indexed in the real estate records, mortgage or land contract modifications and subordination agreements all need the full legal description, and a modification adds the original's document number.

Staff don't draft papers, keep blank deed forms or opine on legal soundness. You can write your own or use an attorney or title company. For return questions, contact the Department of Revenue at (608) 266-1594 or eRETR@revenue.wi.gov.

Allow three to five business days for recording, handled in arrival order, and one to two weeks for the original to come back by post. Because nothing is recorded instantly, leave slack before a closing date. To check on a pending document, email RODrecordings@milwaukeecountywi.gov or call (414) 278-4005.

If a cash buyer wants a quick close, ask the closing agent when the deed gets to the Register of Deeds and whether any return exemption fits your transfer.

sections.h2: Removing a deceased owner from the deed
sections.html:
Record a termination of decedent's interest. Where a deed lists both spouses, you file form HT-110, a transfer return claiming s. 77.25(11) for passage by will, descent or survivorship, a copy of the deed already of record, and $30. The county has dropped its old requirement for a tax bill copy or death certificate.

A recorded transfer on death document works the same way, only with form TOD-110 and the s. 77.25(11m) exemption. Forms and instructions are posted by the Wisconsin Register of Deeds Association. If you're selling an inherited house, check with the title company on whether this filing must precede closing.

Changing ownership any other way, for example adding or dropping a name, means a fresh deed with its own return. The office can't write it.

This free online service emails you when your exact name shows up as grantor or grantee on a recorded document. It can't stop fraud, but it gives early warning if a deed or mortgage appears that you never signed. It suits owners of rentals, vacant homes and inherited houses waiting for sale.

sections.h2: Selling in a split owner and renter county
sections.html: The county is almost evenly split between owners and renters. The owner-occupied rate is 49.9 percent, the median owner-occupied home is valued at $230,700 and median gross rent is $1,101. The county has 392,399 households and 429,425 housing units. These are county-wide numbers; your own city or village treasurer can supply the actual tax bill before you price the house.

Staff can't advise you legally, but the county points to two resources. The Marquette Volunteer Legal Clinic offers free, confidential, brief advice at House of Peace Community Center, 1702 W. Walnut Street, on Tuesdays from 4 to 6 p.m., with sign-in from 3:30 p.m. Its number is (414) 933-1300. The Lawyer Referral and Information Service takes calls Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m.

faqs.a: $30 a document, any page count, with a transfer fee added on most sales. Plats cost $25 to $50, and condominium plats need a separate $100 review check. Pay by cash, check or money order.

faqs.q: What transfer fee does a seller pay?
faqs.a: Thirty cents per $100 of value, the same as $3 per $1,000, set by Wis. Stat. 77.22. It's taken from the seller as the deed is filed. Exempt transfers, like those by will or foreclosure, pay nothing.
No. Every conveyance needs one, and the office treats the receipt as mandatory. An exempt transfer still files a return that states the exemption.

faqs.q: When does the original come back?
faqs.a: It's mailed to the return name and address on the document, one to two weeks after the three to five days of recording. Need proof sooner? Buy a certified copy when you record.

faqs.q: Can this office help with tax bills?
faqs.a: No, it only records documents and collects the transfer fee. Contact the treasurer of the city or village where the house is for balances and payoffs.
